name: Daria Kowalski

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI firms, unions or government. What you say is confidential. What does your workday involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and manage eight people who resolve royalty disputes at a large music-streaming company. We compare play reports, contract terms and payment statements when an artist says the money is wrong. I have an MBA and lead the most difficult cases in our office; I can usually find the missing report before the lawyers need it. I use AI every day to compare files and draft a timeline, then check the contract and speak to the artist’s manager.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My husband drives a school minibus, and our children are ten and sixteen. We have a mortgage and less than a month of expenses saved. My pay is low for a senior manager because this local office has held wages down, and there are few similar music jobs nearby. I know I’m good at this, but the next bill does not care what I know.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the team AI Plateau means a quicker way to sort routine reports. We still need to explain a wrong royalty payment in words the artist can check.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my own job to hold, but the school minibus stops during holidays and our reserve is thin. One missing month of that wage would make the mortgage difficult. Even a small software saving could mean the company leaves a case-handler vacancy open.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the double-check on corrected royalty statements and use my existing AI tool to flag missing report dates. If a small feature arrives, I’d test it against fifteen settled disputes before changing the payment workflow. We would put the next holiday bonus, if it arrives, into the mortgage buffer instead of replacing our sofa.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the household bills. The AI picture is mild, but the minibus does not run every week of the year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which settled dispute would you test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A singer was paid for one version of a song but not the live recording. Our royalty report combined the studio song and its live recording, but the contract paid them separately. I found the missing line after the artist called.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Can the bonus really build a buffer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if it is paid. I would not budget from an announcement, and we have no spare cash to move this month. My husband and I would check the payslip before moving a coin.

say: **AI Plateau** speeds routine reports but still needs an explainable royalty correction.
I would keep the **statement double-check** for artists.
think: My job looks **steady**, but minibus holidays can cut household income.
An unfilled **case vacancy** could add work to our team.
do: **Keep** two checks on corrected royalty statements in 2026.
**Test** a feature on fifteen settled disputes before workflow changes.
**Put** the next bonus into mortgage savings only if actually paid.
feel: I feel **anxious** about bills despite limited AI change.
S0.quote: Our royalty report combined the studio song and its live recording, but the contract paid them separately.
fieldNote: Her **senior skill** does not erase a thin reserve and school-holiday minibus income gap.
The **bonus plan** is explicitly conditional on a payslip, not money already in hand.

steps.text: Keep two checks on corrected royalty statements
Test feature against fifteen settled artist payment disputes
Put bonus into mortgage buffer only after it is paid

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say Steady Disruption could write replies, check plays, plan payments and answer routine artist questions. I would use the new tools, but I would count repeat disputes before saying they saved money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Privately, those tasks fill our week. I am better than most people here at finding a missing play report, yet the company could cut handlers and ask software to do the first pass. My manager post might stay, but if my team shrinks I could lose hours or pay at the same time the minibus is quiet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This quarter I’d pilot the approved discrepancy checker on twenty closed cases, with each handler marking a missed payment. I’d ask for a paid session with the company’s data team to learn how it joins different song versions, and take it if offered in work hours. If our office loses posts, I’d apply for a nearby licensing manager opening only if its pay covers our mortgage and the schedule fits the children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious. I like the tool, but a faster report is not the same as a stable household wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the pilot count?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Wrongly merged songs, missing live recordings and artists who have to call twice. One good-looking total can conceal a small artist who received nothing. I would show the unpaid amount beside the speed result.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why licensing?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know enough contract terms to ask a better question than a first-year hire. I have not managed a licensing team, though. I would read the job description and actual wage before applying.

say: **Royalty AI** needs repeat-dispute and unpaid-amount measures.
I would not call a faster report a **saving** if artists still call twice.
think: Handlers could be cut, and my **hours or pay** might shrink too.
The minibus’s holiday gap makes **household wages** fragile.
do: **Pilot** the approved checker on twenty closed cases this quarter.
**Take** a paid data-team session if offered during work hours.
**Apply** for licensing only if pay and family schedule fit.
feel: I feel **anxious** about pay shrinking despite strong case skills.
S1.quote: One good-looking total can conceal a small artist who received nothing.
fieldNote: She uses **daily AI** to find discrepancies while privately fearing reduced hours or pay.
Her **licensing fallback** is a possible job, not a skill she claims to have already mastered.

steps.text: Pilot approved checker on twenty settled disputes and mark unpaid amounts
Take paid data-team session only if offered during work hours
Apply for licensing vacancy only if mortgage pay and family schedule work

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2028 could compare contracts, count plays and draft every royalty answer cheaply. We need a clear date for staffing and a person who can reverse a wrong payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full thinking AI in 2028 could do almost all my work despite how good I am at it. Robots capable of hands-on work arrive around 2031, but there is no physical shelter in our office. I expect the local disputes team to be cut, and my manager post is likely to go. My husband’s term-time minibus wage cannot cover the mortgage alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Tomorrow I’d ask the regional director for written cut and severance figures, then my husband and I would list the bills that cannot wait. In 2027 I’d apply for the posted licensing job only if net pay after travel covers our mortgage and the hours work for our younger child. If AGI arrives in 2028 and I’m cut, I’d accept a confirmed offer; otherwise I’d ask the lender about a costed payment plan before missing a bill.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed. My skill has a name, but the savings account barely has a balance.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would licensing last?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Its writing, checking and contract work could face AGI in 2028 too. A licensing desk is a job I can apply for now, not a safe island. I would ask which decisions a person still signs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would your children hear?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our sixteen-year-old would want the numbers, and our ten-year-old would ask whether we are moving. I would say we have no offer yet and will keep school the same for now. My husband and I would not change their routine on a rumour.

say: **AGI by 2028** needs cut dates and a human payment appeal.
I would ask for **severance figures**, not a vague reassurance.
think: Disputes and licensing desk work face **2028 AGI**, before unrelated hands-on robots around 2031.
I expect **my post** to go; one minibus wage cannot cover the mortgage.
do: **Ask** the director tomorrow for written dates and severance.
**Apply** in 2027 for licensing only if net pay covers mortgage and child hours.
**Accept** a confirmed licensing offer after 2028 only if net mortgage pay and child hours work.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by likely post loss and almost no reserve.
S2.quote: My skill has a name, but the savings account barely has a balance.
fieldNote: She expects **her own job loss** and has little saved despite being a leading manager with an MBA.
The **lender call** is a cost check, while a licensing post remains exposed to AGI in 2028.

steps.text: Apply for licensing role only if pay after travel covers mortgage and child hours
Accept confirmed licensing offer after 2028 only if net mortgage pay and child hours work

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives us five years to decide who listens when an artist says the payment is wrong. I would want that person to have the power to correct the statement, not only read a script.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My dispute reports and an artist-relations manager’s emails could still be done by AGI in 2031. Robots able to do hands-on work arrive around 2034, but those are not our jobs. Five years lets me learn more face-to-face relationship work while I earn, though no one has promised that post.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From January 2027 I’d take part in two paid artist meetings with our relations lead if my director covers my dispute desk. I’d ask the lead to let me explain one wrong statement to an artist and correct my approach afterwards. After 2031 I’d apply for a relations vacancy only if it still has payment authority, covers the mortgage after travel and works with our family hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious. I can improve artist-facing skills, but I cannot feed my children a future job title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say in that meeting?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show the artist the missing live version, the contract line and the correction date. I know the numbers; I need practice delivering bad news without sounding like a form letter. The lead could tell me where I lose the person.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if meetings happen after your shift?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for paid time and desk cover. My husband may be driving a school route and the younger child still needs us. I would not volunteer unpaid evenings for a job that might not open.

say: **Five years** allows paid meetings with artists before I move into a different role.
An artist-relations manager must have **payment-correction authority**, not only a script for explaining errors.
think: Dispute reports and relations emails face **2031 AGI**, before unrelated robots around 2034.
A paid **relations vacancy** is uncertain despite time to practise.
do: **Join** two paid artist meetings from January 2027 only with desk cover and younger-child care.
**Explain** one wrong statement under relations-lead review during paid time.
**Apply** after 2031 only for relations work with authority, net mortgage pay and family hours.
feel: I feel **anxious** about a possible desk loss, with time to test people work.
S3.quote: I can improve artist-facing skills, but I cannot feed my children a future job title.
fieldNote: She distinguishes **face-to-face practice** from a claim that artist-relations emails escape AGI.
The **paid meetings** need desk cover and childcare; a later vacancy needs authority and mortgage-covering pay.

steps.text: Join two paid artist meetings only with dispute-desk cover and younger-child care
Explain wrong statement under relations-lead review during paid meeting
Apply after 2031 for relations role only with payment authority net mortgage pay and family hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives employers a decade to tell staff which payment jobs remain and what they pay. I would ask for real posts, not a library of courses.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: By 2036 our children will be about twenty and twenty-six. If both wages keep coming, we could reduce the mortgage and build more than a few weeks of savings. My royalty and relations paperwork still faces AGI in 2036, while hands-on robots arrive around 2039 in other work. A longer runway helps, but this month’s bills remain close.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the statement double-check and put any actual bonus into savings after mortgage and school costs clear. I’d review posted artist-relations and licensing roles each year. Before 2036 I’d take a paid relations assignment only with my wage protected; after AGI arrives I’d stay only while the job can correct payments and pays our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the bank balance today. I could be in a better place in ten years, but I will not count money that has not arrived.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much would the bonus help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A bonus could buy a month of bills, but only if it is paid and the minibus has not lost too many weeks. I would check the account after the mortgage and school costs. I would not spend a promised bonus twice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move to a music city?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for an actual offer after comparing rent or house costs with the pay. The children are in school now, and we cannot afford a speculative move. By 2036 they will be grown, so the choice may look different.

say: A **decade** should bring actual payment jobs with wages attached.
I would ask for **posted roles**, not only courses.
think: Two wages could reduce the **mortgage** and grow savings if they hold.
Royalty and relations paperwork face **2036 AGI**, before unrelated robots around 2039.
do: **Save** an actual bonus only after mortgage, school bills and minibus wages allow it.
**Take** paid relations work only with protected wages; stay after 2036 only with correction authority and bill pay.
feel: I feel **anxious** about today’s balance despite a longer warning.
S4.quote: I would not spend a promised bonus twice.
fieldNote: Her **thin reserve** and uncertain holiday income keep present anxiety alive even with ten years.
The **bonus saving** waits for actual payment, mortgage, school costs and minibus hours.

steps.text: Keep two checks on corrected royalty statements in 2026
Save only paid bonus after mortgage school costs and minibus income are known
Take paid relations assignment only with protected wage and actual opening
Stay after 2036 only with payment authority and bill-covering wage

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because our local disputes desk could close before another music job appears. A written date, severance and paid artist-facing work would help. My MBA is not an extra month in the bank.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the singer whose live version vanished from the payment report whether a quick answer helped. A correct total can still hide a missing song. Someone has to put the live recording back in the account.

headlineQuote: A correct total can still hide a missing song.
portrait: **Daria, 43**, is an MBA-trained senior royalties-dispute manager leading eight people at a large streaming company.
Her **low pay**, minibus-driver husband, mortgage, two children and under-one-month reserve leave few local music jobs.
She uses **AI daily** to trace payments but checks contracts and speaks with artists before approving corrections.
She is **anxious** even in AI Plateau, expects a fast local desk cut and tests paid artist-facing work conditionally.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could close her local disputes desk before another suitable music post appears.
whatWouldHelp: A written **cut date**, severance and paid artist-facing work would help.
